NGA.hook: The most populous country in Africa — about one in six Africans is Nigerian — and Nollywood releases more films a year than Hollywood.
NGA.place: On the Gulf of Guinea at the inner corner of the West African bulge.

NER.hook: Has the youngest population on Earth — around half of Niger is under fifteen.
NER.place: Landlocked and mostly Sahara, sitting directly on top of Nigeria. The two names are the mix-up to watch.

MLI.hook: Timbuktu was a university town when Oxford was new, and its medieval ruler Mansa Musa may have been the richest person who ever lived.
MLI.place: Landlocked across the western Sahel, with the Niger river arcing through its middle.

BFA.hook: Its name was invented in 1984 and means land of upright people — stitched together from two different local languages.
BFA.place: Landlocked directly above Ghana and Ivory Coast, below Mali and Niger.

CIV.hook: Grows roughly 40% of the world's cocoa — more than the next two countries combined. Also answers to Côte d'Ivoire.
CIV.place: On the Gulf of Guinea between Ghana and Liberia.

GHA.hook: The first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence, in 1957 — and Lake Volta is the largest reservoir on Earth by surface area.
GHA.place: On the Gulf of Guinea, between Ivory Coast and Togo.

TGO.hook: One of Africa's narrowest countries — about 110km wide but 550km long, a strip you can drive across in two hours.
TGO.place: A thin ribbon between Ghana and Benin, running north from the Gulf of Guinea.

BEN.hook: The birthplace of Vodun, which is an official religion here — and home of the Dahomey kingdom's all-female regiment.
BEN.place: A narrow strip running north from the Gulf of Guinea, between Togo and Nigeria.

SEN.hook: Reaches the westernmost point of mainland Africa, and almost completely surrounds another country — The Gambia.
SEN.place: The Atlantic tip of the West African bulge, wrapped around The Gambia on three sides.

GMB.hook: The smallest country in mainland Africa — a ribbon of land either side of one river, nowhere more than 50km wide.
GMB.place: Following the Gambia river inland, enclosed by Senegal on every side but the Atlantic.

GNB.hook: The Bijagós archipelago off its coast is 88 islands, only about twenty of them inhabited — and a biosphere reserve.
GNB.place: A small Atlantic country tucked between Senegal and Guinea.

GIN.hook: Holds the world's largest bauxite reserves — and the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers all rise in its highlands.
GIN.place: On the Atlantic below Senegal, between Guinea-Bissau and Sierra Leone.

SLE.hook: Freetown sits on one of the largest natural harbours in the world, which is why freed slaves were resettled there in 1792.
SLE.place: On the Atlantic coast between Guinea and Liberia.

LBR.hook: Founded by freed American slaves in 1847, making it Africa's oldest republic — and more of the world's shipping flies its flag than almost any other.
LBR.place: On the Atlantic below Sierra Leone, west of Ivory Coast.

MRT.hook: Runs one of the longest trains in the world — up to 2.5km of iron ore across the desert, with passengers riding on top of the load.
MRT.place: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic, above Senegal and west of Mali.

CPV.hook: Ten volcanic islands that were completely uninhabited until Portuguese ships arrived in 1456 — everyone there descends from later arrivals.
CPV.place: An Atlantic archipelago about 570km west of Senegal, out on its own.
